question.text: As an option approaches its expiry date, what generally happens to its time value?

answer.text: Time value decreases and approaches zero at expiry (time decay)
Time value increases as there is more urgency to trade
Time value remains constant throughout the option's life
Time value becomes negative near expiry

explanation.text: The Logic: Time value of an option decreases with the passage of time and gradually falls to zero at expiry. Options tend to lose time value each day as expiry approaches, so at expiry the option is worth only its intrinsic value (if any). The Trap: Time value does not stay constant and it does not turn negative. It simply erodes towards zero as the option moves closer to expiry. Note: Because of this time decay, time value works against the option buyer and in favour of the option seller.
